title: Replace advisory allow/deny booleans with a sealed execution capability
finding: Execution authorization is represented as serializable booleans and a conventional `if` branch rather than a required capability. `EffectPreflightReportV1` exposes `blocked/advisory_only/commit_eligible`, `EffectCommitDecisionV1` exposes `commit_authorized`, `verification-policy` exposes `PolicyDecision::allows_execution() -> bool`, and `forge-pilot` branches on that boolean before calling execution.
why_it_matters: This is policy by convention. A downstream caller can bypass the branch and still reach effectful code. The spec requires hard gates, not strongly-worded JSON.
evidence: effect-runtime/src/effect.rs; verification-policy/src/lib.rs:272; forge-pilot/src/loop_runner.rs:440,540,705; llm-tool-runtime/src/contracts.rs
required_changes: Introduce a sealed runtime-only `CommitToken` / `ExecutionPermit` minted only after policy + approval + verification-plan checks. All effectful execution APIs must require that token. Artifacts remain serializable receipts; the token is the runtime enforcement object.
acceptance: No effectful path can be invoked with only booleans or raw strings. `rg -n "CommitToken|ExecutionPermit|ApprovalGrant" verification-policy llm-tool-runtime forge-pilot effect-runtime` returns owned types and use-sites; direct execute signatures without a permit are gone.
proof: rg -n "allows_execution\(|commit_authorized|approval_token" effect-runtime verification-policy llm-tool-runtime forge-pilot && cargo test -p llm-tool-runtime -p forge-pilot
touches: verification-policy/src/lib.rs; verification-policy/src/permit.rs (new); llm-tool-runtime/src/contracts.rs; llm-tool-runtime/src/runtime.rs; forge-pilot/src/loop_runner.rs; forge-pilot/src/act.rs; effect-runtime/src/effect.rs; stack-ids/src/ids.rs

title: Replace `ToolCtx.approval_token: Option<String>` with a typed constitutional grant
finding: `llm-tool-runtime` already has decent enum discipline, but the actual approval carrier is still `Option<String>`. That means the critical approval path is stringly and forgeable by construction.
why_it_matters: A free-form approval token undercuts the very enforcement point that should be strongest. It must be tied to scope, effect class, constitution citation, expiry, and decision lineage.
evidence: llm-tool-runtime/src/contracts.rs:262-291; llm-tool-runtime/src/runtime.rs:33-45; llm-tool-runtime/src/starter_tools.rs:401,493-514
spec_anchors: V9 §5 execution evidence; V11 §8 proof-governed promotion; V16 §8 budget/disclosure/suspension; ENDSTATE §8 and §10
required_changes: Define a typed `ApprovalGrant` or reuse the `CommitToken` family. Carry scope, effect/action class, approver lineage, expiry, decision id, and constitution citation. Read-only fast paths may remain tokenless only if the tool descriptor is provably read-only and non-promoting.
acceptance: `ToolCtx` no longer contains `approval_token: Option<String>`. Approval evaluation accepts a typed grant. Destructive tools cannot be invoked with raw strings.
proof: rg -n "approval_token: Option<String>" llm-tool-runtime/src && cargo test -p llm-tool-runtime
touches: llm-tool-runtime/src/contracts.rs; llm-tool-runtime/src/runtime.rs; llm-tool-runtime/src/starter_tools.rs; forge-pilot/src/act.rs; verification-policy/src/lib.rs

title: Eliminate stringly typed controlled vocabularies from governance and control surfaces
